gen-dafont-aaargh-fs-epilogue: Aaargh draws every bowl and stem at one thickness, with a generous entry into the e. Epilogue brings a tall-bodied lowercase and a wire-like skeleton, which is the quality that makes the pairing memorable.
gen-dafont-aaargh-fs-quicksand: Quicksand has tall bowls like blown glass bulbs. Its bars keep an identical thickness, and its terminals stop well clear of the stem, so Aaargh above it looks heavier and more commanding.
gen-dafont-aaargh-fs-spline-sans: Approachable and contemporary, Spline Sans leaves wide gaps between curve ends and stems. Vertical and horizontal strokes carry identical weight, so paragraphs under Aaargh's commanding heading keep a smooth, unfussy texture line after line.
gen-dafont-aaargh-fs-synonym: Dependable is the word for Synonym, a plain stripe of constant ink with generous openings in every curve. Aaargh does the loud work, strong and commanding, and Synonym handles the quiet job of being read.
gen-dafont-aaargh-general-sans: General Sans keeps a steady pen pressure with an x-height that fills the line and smooth paths around every bend. Next to Aaargh it feels cooler and more composed.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-alegreya: Aaargh is strong and unshaded, with no quill-like tapering anywhere. It earns its keep big and brief, while Alegreya adds a literary serif voice with wide apertures and lightly flexed contrast.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-alegreya-sc: Aaargh brings a wire-like monoline skeleton and a commanding presence, with a generous entry into the e's eye. Alegreya SC follows traditionally, its wide-open s and lighter horizontals keeping a long passage dignified.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-alike-angular: Blunt, constant strokes like bent wire, with bowls and stems at matching weight. Alike Angular carries a subtle thick and thin cadence, so a long passage feels held open, traditional and authoritative.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-alyamama: Aaargh traces a constant-width outline you could follow with a finger, strong and commanding. And Alyamama adds refined serif joins that thin gently without turning spindly, so the two sit comfortably together on the page.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-ancizar-serif: Editorial in spirit, Ancizar Serif sets modest contrast like lightly engraved brass beneath Aaargh's plain, unshaded line. Ancizar Serif brings a mellow swing from thick to thin that softens the heading's commanding stance.
